chapters.title: Unit 1: From the Ancient World to the Modern World

lessons.title: The Ancient World: India
lessons.notes_html:
The Maurya Empire

The Maurya Empire was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE. It lasted for about 140 years (from 321 BCE to about 185 BCE). Chandragupta ended the rule of the Nanda Raja and established the empire.

His adviser was Chanakya (Kautilya), the author of the famous book Arthashastra. After Chandragupta, his son Bindusara ruled (298 to 272 BCE). The most famous Maurya ruler was Ashoka, the grandson of Chandragupta, who became king in about 269 BCE. After the Kalinga war, Ashoka adopted Buddhism and preached Dhamma. His empire included a large part of northern India.

How the Maurya Empire Progressed

FactorWhat happenedEffect
SocialSociety was divided into seven classes: philosophers, farmers, soldiers, herdsmen, craftsmen, officials and councillors; city life and temple-building progressedAn organised society and urban culture arose
PoliticalCentral government and laws according to the ArthashastraA strong and stable empire was established
EconomicPeace was established; agriculture and trade were encouraged; coins were usedProsperity and wealth increased
AdministrativeThe empire was divided into four provinces, each with a royal governorControl and order over the large empire were maintained

Alexander the Great in India

Alexander set out from Macedonia, passed through Persia, crossed the Hindu Kush and entered north-western India (the area of today's Pakistan). He fought Raja Porus at the river Jhelum. When his army refused to advance further, he turned back.

The Gupta Empire — The Golden Age

In the Gupta period people lived in peace and prosperity. People turned towards Hinduism, but other religions had freedom. There was great progress in knowledge, art, science, technology, astronomy and mathematics, and splendid progress in art and literature. Trade grew and gold coins were used. That is why the Gupta period is called the golden age of the history of India.

After the death of Chandragupta II the decline of the Gupta Empire began: regions slowly separated, the later rulers were not capable of governing, and the empire was destroyed by local and foreign attacks.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Maurya Empire?
mcqs.why: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire in 321 BCE. He ended the rule of the Nanda Raja and set up the empire. Ashoka was his grandson, and Chanakya was his adviser.

mcqs.q: In which year was the Maurya Empire founded?
mcqs.why: The Maurya Empire was founded in 321 BCE. The year 269 BCE is when Ashoka became king, and about 185 BCE is when the empire ended.

mcqs.q: Who was the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya?
mcqs.why: Ashoka was the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya. Bindusara was Chandragupta's son, so Ashoka was Bindusara's son and Chandragupta's grandson.

mcqs.q: For about how long did the Maurya Empire last?
mcqs.why: The Maurya Empire lasted for about 140 years, from 321 BCE to about 185 BCE. This is the generally accepted historical estimate.

mcqs.q: Ashoka became king in about which year?
mcqs.why: Ashoka became king in about 269 BCE and ruled until 232 BCE. He is the most famous Maurya ruler, known for adopting Buddhism after the Kalinga war.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the Arthashastra?
mcqs.why: Chanakya, also called Kautilya, was the adviser of Chandragupta Maurya. He wrote the Arthashastra, the famous book on government and laws.

mcqs.q: Into how many provinces was the Maurya Empire divided?
mcqs.why: The Maurya Empire was divided into four provinces, and a royal governor was appointed in each province. This helped the king keep control and order over the large empire.

mcqs.q: After which war did Ashoka adopt Buddhism?
mcqs.why: After the Kalinga war, Ashoka adopted Buddhism and preached Dhamma. The bloodshed of that war changed his heart and his policies.

mcqs.q: The Gupta period is called ______ of the history of India.
mcqs.why: The Gupta period is called the golden age of the history of India. There was splendid progress in knowledge, art, science, astronomy, mathematics and literature in that period.

mcqs.q: Which coins were used in the Gupta Empire?
mcqs.why: Trade grew in the Gupta Empire and gold coins were used. The use of gold coins shows the wealth and prosperity of that period.

lessons.title: Iran (500 BCE to 500 CE)
lessons.notes_html:
The Foundation of the Iranian Empire

The foundation of the Iranian Empire was laid in 550 BCE by Cyrus the Great. Before this, the tribal people of Iran were under the Median rulers.

How Cyrus Treated the Conquered People

Cyrus treated the conquered people with tolerance and respect:

  • He respected their local customs and religions.
  • He rebuilt their temples and places of worship.
  • In 538 BCE he allowed the Jews to return to their own country.
  • He did not allow slavery in his empire.
  • He allowed the people of conquered regions to keep their own laws and rulers.

Darius and His System of Government

Darius kept his large empire united by strong methods:

  • He divided the empire into 20 provinces (satrapies) and appointed a governor (satrap) in each.
  • He appointed a separate military commander and tax collector in each province.
  • His spies were called "the eyes and ears of the king".
  • He built the famous Royal Road, which went from Susa in Iran to Sardis in Anatolia and was 1677 miles long.
  • He introduced uniform coins throughout the empire.

Zoroastrianism

The religion of Zoroaster, Zoroastrianism, gave people answers to questions about their problems. Its teaching is that a war between the spirits of good and evil is going on in the world, and every person should support goodness.

Wars Between Iran and Greece

WarYearWinner
Battle of Marathon490 BCEGreeks
Battle of Thermopylae480 BCEIranians
Naval Battle of Salamis480 BCEGreeks
Battle of Plataea479 BCEGreeks
Battle of Mycale479 BCEGreeks

Effects of the Iranian Empire

  • Social: people of different nations and tribes began living together in one large empire.
  • Political: organised administration was established through the satrapy system and the Royal Road.
  • Cultural: there was progress in architecture, carving and the art of coins.
  • Religious: because of the tolerance of the rulers, different religions lived together and Zoroastrianism spread.

After Alexander the Great conquered Iran, the Achaemenid Empire came to an end. After Alexander's death, his empire was divided among his generals and Iran came into the hands of the Seleucid rulers. Greek and Iranian civilisations then blended together.

mcqs.q: Who laid the foundation of the Iranian Empire in 550 BCE?
mcqs.why: Cyrus the Great laid the foundation of the Iranian Empire in 550 BCE. Darius came later and organised the empire, while Zoroaster was a religious teacher, not a king.

mcqs.q: The Royal Road built by Darius went from Susa to which city?
mcqs.why: The Royal Road went from Susa in Iran to Sardis in Anatolia. It was 1677 miles long and helped Darius control his large empire.

mcqs.q: How long was the Royal Road?
mcqs.why: The Royal Road was 1677 miles long. Through this road, orders, armies and taxes could move quickly between the king and the distant provinces.

mcqs.q: Into how many provinces (satrapies) did Darius divide his empire?
mcqs.why: Darius divided the empire into 20 provinces called satrapies. He appointed a governor, called a satrap, in each province to keep the empire united.

mcqs.q: The spies of Darius were called _______.
options: The eyes and ears of the king
mcqs.why: Darius appointed spies who were called 'the eyes and ears of the king'. They informed the king about everything happening in the provinces.

mcqs.q: What is the main teaching of Zoroastrianism?
options: There are many gods of nature
A war between good and evil is going on, and every person should support goodness
mcqs.why: Zoroastrianism, the teaching of Zoroaster, says a war between the spirits of good and evil is going on in the world. Every person should support goodness in this struggle.

mcqs.q: Who won the Battle of Marathon in 490 BCE?
mcqs.why: The Greeks won the Battle of Marathon in 490 BCE. In most of the wars of 490–479 BCE the Greeks won; the Iranians won only at Thermopylae.

mcqs.q: Who won the Battle of Thermopylae in 480 BCE?
mcqs.why: The Iranians won the Battle of Thermopylae in 480 BCE. In the same year, however, the Greeks defeated Iran in the naval Battle of Salamis.

mcqs.q: In 538 BCE, Cyrus allowed which people to return to their own country?
mcqs.why: In 538 BCE Cyrus allowed the Jews to return to their own country. This shows his tolerance: he also respected local customs and rebuilt temples of conquered people.

mcqs.q: After the death of Alexander the Great, Iran came into the hands of which rulers?
mcqs.why: After Alexander's death, his large empire was divided among his generals. The region of Iran came into the hands of the Seleucid rulers.

lessons.title: Transition to the Modern World
lessons.notes_html:
The Medieval Period

The medieval period of history in Europe continued from 400 CE to 1500 CE. The Middle Ages are also called the dark age of history. In this period the feudal system existed — a system based on the ownership of land (fief), which included kings, nobles, farmers and labourers. A terrible plague, the Black Death, spread in Europe and millions of people died.

The Crusades

The Crusades were the wars of the Cross — wars fought by the Christians to take back the Holy Land (Jerusalem).

CrusadeYearsResult
First Crusade1096–1099 CEThe Christians captured Jerusalem
Second Crusade1147–1149 CEThe Muslims remained successful
Third Crusade1189–1192 CEUnder Salahuddin Ayyubi the Muslims took back Jerusalem; then peace was made
Fourth Crusade1202–1204 CEThe Christians attacked Constantinople

The Umayyads and the Spread of Islam

The Umayyad rulers (661 to 750 CE) spread Islam through conquests — the Islamic empire grew from Spain to Central Asia. Through strong government and administration, and through trade and contacts, Islam reached different countries.

The End of the Abbasids

The Abbasid government came to an end because of several factors:

  • The opposition of the non-Arab Muslims, who were treated as second-class citizens and had to pay more tax.
  • Their revolt in 747 CE and the movement under Abu al-Abbas.
  • The Mongol attack in 1258 CE, in which Baghdad was destroyed.

The Rise of the Ottoman Empire

The Ottoman Empire developed because of the Ghazis (brave horsemen with light weapons), the Janissaries (the best-trained army, made from slaves obtained from conquered countries), a strong army and weapons. In 1453 CE the Ottomans conquered Constantinople, after which the Ottoman Empire became a great power and spread into half of Europe.

mcqs.q: The medieval period of history in Europe continued from _______.
mcqs.why: The medieval period in Europe continued from 400 CE to 1500 CE. This long period is also called the Middle Ages.

mcqs.q: The 'dark age' of history is attributed to which period?
mcqs.why: The dark age of history is attributed to the Middle Ages, that is, the medieval period (400 CE to 1500 CE). Feudalism and the Black Death belong to this period.

mcqs.q: The Crusades were wars fought to take back which place?
mcqs.why: The Crusades were the wars of the Cross, fought by the Christians to take back the Holy Land, Jerusalem. They began in 1096 CE.

mcqs.q: The feudal system was based on _______.
mcqs.why: The feudal system refers to the ownership of land (fief) and the social and political system based on it. It included kings, nobles, farmers and labourers.

mcqs.q: Which disease spread in Europe and killed millions of people?
mcqs.why: The Black Death, a plague, spread in Europe during the medieval period. Because of it, millions of people died.

mcqs.q: The Umayyad rulers ruled from _______.
mcqs.why: The Umayyad rulers ruled from 661 to 750 CE. In their time the Islamic empire grew from Spain to Central Asia.

mcqs.q: Baghdad was destroyed by the Mongols in which year?
mcqs.why: The Mongols attacked in 1258 CE and destroyed Baghdad. With this attack, the government of the Abbasid dynasty came to an end.

mcqs.q: Constantinople was conquered by the Ottomans in _______.
mcqs.why: Constantinople was conquered in 1453 CE. After this victory the Ottoman Empire became a great power and spread into half of Europe.

mcqs.q: Who were the Janissaries?
options: The best-trained Ottoman army made from slaves from conquered countries
mcqs.why: The Janissaries were the best-trained army of the Ottoman Empire, made from slaves obtained from conquered countries. Together with the Ghazis, they helped the empire grow.

mcqs.q: In the Third Crusade, the Muslims who took back Jerusalem were led by _______.
mcqs.why: In the Third Crusade (1189–1192 CE), under the leadership of Salahuddin Ayyubi, the Muslims took back Jerusalem. After that, peace was made between the two sides.

Timeline of Unit 1: Ancient to Modern

Why the Royal Road Helped Darius

Through the Royal Road, Darius's orders and army could quickly reach distant provinces. Taxes and information could also arrive quickly, trade grew, and people's contact with the government became strong. Therefore, control over the large empire was maintained.

Why Empires Fall: Incapable Rulers

In the Iranian Empire, in the period of weak and incapable rulers, the governors began to revolt, taxes decreased and economic problems grew; then Alexander's attack ended the empire. The same happened in the Gupta Empire: after the death of Chandragupta II, incapable rulers came, regions began to separate, and the empire was destroyed.

True Teachings of Zoroastrianism

People had questions about good and evil and the suffering in the world, and Zoroaster gave answers to those questions. The true teachings are: faith in one God, Ahura Mazda; a war between the spirits of good and evil is going on in the world and every person should support goodness; and one should adopt good thoughts, good words and good deeds.

Spread of the Ottoman Empire

In 1326 CE a small empire began under a Turkish chief, Osman. In 1350 CE the Turks attacked Europe, and in 1389 CE came the Battle of Kosovo. In 1453 CE Constantinople was conquered. Then the empire spread to the Middle East (Syria, Iraq, Hijaz), North Africa (Egypt) and Eastern Europe (up to Hungary).

Why Did the Muslims Decline in the Fifteenth Century?

  • Internal differences and weak governments
  • The Mongol attacks and the fall of Baghdad (1258 CE)
  • Change in trade routes
  • New scientific and military progress in Europe

mcqs.q: According to the Unit 1 timeline, the Gupta Empire began in _______.
mcqs.why: The timeline of Unit 1 shows the beginning of the Gupta Empire in 320 CE. The year 321 BCE belongs to the Maurya Empire, which is a different empire of ancient India.

mcqs.q: The Umayyad government lasted from _______.
mcqs.why: In the Unit 1 timeline, the Umayyad government is 661–750 CE. The period 750–1258 CE is the Abbasid government, which came after the Umayyads.

mcqs.q: How did the Royal Road help Darius maintain power?
options: It was used only for trade fairs
Orders and armies could quickly reach distant provinces
It kept enemies out of Iran
mcqs.why: Through the Royal Road, Darius's orders and army could quickly reach distant provinces, and taxes and information arrived quickly too. This strong contact kept control over the large empire.

mcqs.q: Which empire is given as another example of destruction by incapable rulers?
mcqs.why: The Gupta Empire is the other example: after the death of Chandragupta II, incapable rulers came, regions began to separate, and the empire was destroyed.

mcqs.q: In Zoroastrianism, the one God is called _______.
mcqs.why: The true teaching of Zoroastrianism is faith in one God, Ahura Mazda. It also teaches that a war between good and evil is going on and every person should support goodness.

mcqs.q: According to Zoroastrianism, a person should adopt _______.
options: Good thoughts, good words and good deeds
mcqs.why: Zoroastrianism teaches good thoughts, good words and good deeds. By following these, a person supports goodness in the war between good and evil.

mcqs.q: The Ottoman Empire began in 1326 CE under a Turkish chief named _______.
mcqs.why: In 1326 CE a small empire began under a Turkish chief, Osman. The Ottoman Empire takes its name from him and later spread over three continents.

mcqs.q: The Battle of Kosovo was fought in _______.
mcqs.why: The Battle of Kosovo was fought in 1389 CE, during the spread of the Ottoman Empire into Europe. Constantinople was conquered later, in 1453 CE.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a cause of the decline of the Muslims in the fifteenth century?
options: The building of the Royal Road
mcqs.why: Internal differences and weak governments were a main cause of the decline. Other causes were the Mongol attacks, the fall of Baghdad, changed trade routes and new progress in Europe.

mcqs.q: The Crusades began in which year?
mcqs.why: The Crusades began in 1096 CE, with the First Crusade (1096–1099 CE). The fall of Baghdad in 1258 CE and the conquest of Constantinople in 1453 CE came much later.

lessons.title: The Constitution
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Constitution?

The constitution is the basic, necessary and fundamental law of the state. It is the law in which the rules about the organisation, powers and duties of the government of the state are stated.

The Three Institutions of Government

A representative government consists of three institutions:

  • The Executive — runs the government and implements the laws.
  • The Legislature — the law-making body.
  • The Judiciary — the courts that interpret the law.

Sovereignty

Sovereignty means supreme authority. The sovereign is one who does not share his authority with anyone and whose orders cannot be objected to. According to the Constitution of 1973, Pakistan is a sovereign state, and its authority is used through the elected representatives of the people.

The Rule of Law

The rule of law means that no person is above the law. All citizens are equal before the law and all have equal protection of the law. According to Dicey, the world expert on law, the government too is bound by the law, and no one can use authority according to his own will.

Written and Unwritten Constitutions

MeritsDemerits
Unwritten constitutionIt is flexible and can change gradually according to the need of the time; it is based on customs, traditions and court decisionsIt is not written in one book, so the common man does not know about it; the government can use it according to its own will; the protection of rights remains weak

The Constitution of Pakistan

The Constitution of Pakistan consists of 280 articles. It includes 12 parts and 6 schedules, and 23 amendments have been made in it so far.

How the Constitution Protects Fundamental Rights

The constitution gives the citizens of Pakistan fundamental rights: equality before the law, freedom of thought, belief, faith and worship, and freedom to form associations. The condition is that these freedoms are not used against the rights of others and the law.

Supreme CourtParliament
Interprets and protects the constitution; protects the fundamental rights of the citizens; maintains the rule of lawMakes laws for the country; it includes the National Assembly and the Senate; keeps watch over the work of the government

mcqs.q: The basic, necessary and fundamental law of the state is called _______.
mcqs.why: The constitution is the fundamental law of the state. It states the rules about the organisation, powers and duties of the government.

mcqs.q: Which institution of government makes the laws?
mcqs.why: The legislature is the law-making body of the government. The executive implements the laws and the judiciary interprets them through the courts.

mcqs.q: Sovereignty means _______.
mcqs.why: Sovereignty means supreme authority. A sovereign does not share his authority with anyone, and his orders cannot be objected to.

mcqs.q: The Constitution of Pakistan consists of how many articles?
mcqs.why: The Constitution of Pakistan consists of 280 articles. It also includes 12 parts and 6 schedules.

mcqs.q: The rule of law means _______.
options: No person is above the law
The king is above the law
Only rich people follow the law
mcqs.why: The rule of law means no person is above the law. All citizens are equal before the law and all have equal protection of the law.

mcqs.q: According to Dicey, who is also bound by the law?
mcqs.why: According to Dicey, the world expert on law, the government too is bound by the law. No one can use authority according to his own will.

mcqs.q: Which is a merit of an unwritten constitution?
options: It is written in one book
It is flexible and changes gradually with the need of the time
mcqs.why: An unwritten constitution is flexible and can change gradually according to the need of the time. It is based on customs, traditions and court decisions.

mcqs.q: Which is a demerit of an unwritten constitution?
options: It is changed by the courts daily
The common man does not know about it because it is not written in one book
mcqs.why: Because an unwritten constitution is not written in one book, the common man does not know about it. The government can also use it according to its own will, and the protection of rights remains weak.

mcqs.q: What is the work of the Supreme Court?
options: To interpret and protect the constitution
To make laws for the country
mcqs.why: The Supreme Court interprets and protects the constitution. It also protects the fundamental rights of the citizens and maintains the rule of law.

mcqs.q: The Parliament of Pakistan includes _______.
options: The Supreme Court and High Courts
The National Assembly and the Senate
mcqs.why: Parliament makes laws for the country and includes the National Assembly and the Senate. It also keeps watch over the work of the government.

lessons.title: Citizens' Rights and Responsibilities
lessons.notes_html:
Three Kinds of Rights

Kind of rightExamples
Civil rightsLife, freedom, personal safety, property, freedom of expression and worship
Political rightsVoting, forming associations, taking part in elections, becoming a candidate for public office
Economic and social rightsWork, fair wages, education, health, housing and a decent standard of living

Civil rights are especially connected with the citizen's life and freedom. Fundamental rights encourage and motivate a better life, freedom and equality.

Article 25-A: Free Education

According to Article 25-A of the Constitution, providing free and compulsory education to all children from the age of five (5) to sixteen (16) years is the responsibility of the state.

Responsibilities of a Citizen

  • Supporting and defending the constitution
  • Keeping informed about matters affecting society
  • Participating in the democratic process
  • Respecting and obeying the laws
  • Respecting the rights, beliefs and views of other people
  • Participating in the local community
  • Paying income and other taxes on time
  • Respecting the state and local institutions
  • Defending the country when needed

Why Are There Limits on Rights?

Limits and restrictions are placed on rights so that one person's right does not go against another person's right and balance is maintained in society. For example, freedom of expression does not mean harming someone's honour. With every right, respecting the rights of others is also necessary.

Contacting Your Elected Representatives

Citizens contact the elected representatives of their area to tell them what work they have done, to ask them to play a role in some activity, and to tell them their views about education, crime and other problems of the area. Ways of contact are: writing a letter, going to meet them, phoning, or speaking in a gathering.

Advocacy: Insider and Outsider Strategies

  • Insider strategy — direct contact with decision-makers: for example, meeting your representative and talking about the school's problem, or writing him a letter.
  • Outsider strategy — through public pressure: for example, taking out a peaceful rally, writing an article in a newspaper, or running a public campaign.

The strategy of legal consultation and advocacy has nine steps: objective, audience, message, messenger, delivery, resources, differences and concerns, beginning, and assessment and evaluation.

mcqs.q: Civil rights are especially connected with a citizen's life and _______.
mcqs.why: Civil rights are especially connected with the citizen's life and freedom. They include personal safety, property, and freedom of expression and worship.

mcqs.q: According to Article 25-A, the state must provide free and compulsory education to children of which ages?
mcqs.why: Article 25-A declares that providing free and compulsory education to all children from the age of five to sixteen years is the responsibility of the state.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a political right?
options: Right to vote and become a candidate
mcqs.why: Political rights include voting, forming associations, taking part in elections and becoming a candidate for public office. Fair wages and health are economic and social rights.

mcqs.q: Work, fair wages, education and health are examples of _______ rights.
mcqs.why: Economic and social rights include work, fair wages, education, health, housing and a decent standard of living. These rights help a citizen live a better life.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a responsibility of a citizen?
options: Paying income and other taxes on time
mcqs.why: Paying taxes on time is a citizen's responsibility. Other responsibilities include obeying the laws, respecting others' rights and defending the country when needed.

mcqs.q: Why are limits and restrictions placed on rights?
options: So that one person's right does not go against another person's right
mcqs.why: Limits keep balance in society, so one person's right does not harm another person's right. For example, freedom of expression does not mean harming someone's honour.

mcqs.q: Meeting your representative and talking about your school's problem is an example of _______ strategy.
mcqs.why: The insider strategy means direct contact with decision-makers, such as meeting your representative or writing him a letter. The outsider strategy works through public pressure.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an outsider strategy of advocacy?
options: Taking out a peaceful rally and running a public campaign
Writing a letter to your representative
mcqs.why: The outsider strategy works through public pressure, for example a peaceful rally, a newspaper article or a public campaign. Direct meetings and letters are insider strategies.

mcqs.q: What is the first step of the advocacy strategy?
options: Objective — what is to be achieved
mcqs.why: The first of the nine steps of advocacy is the objective: deciding what is to be achieved. After that come the audience, message, messenger and the other steps.

mcqs.q: Fundamental rights encourage and motivate a better life, _______ and equality.
mcqs.why: Fundamental rights encourage a better life, freedom and equality. They protect the citizen's life and liberty and are given by the constitution.

lessons.title: Role of Civil Society Organisations and Active Citizenship
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Volunteer?

A person who works for an organisation without payment of any compensation is called a volunteer. Volunteer activity plays an important role in progress in the global economy.

The Basic Role of Civil Society Organisations

The basic role of a civil society organisation is to limit and regulate the authority of the state. These organisations can also provide a development field for future political leaders.

Roles and Duties of Civil Society Organisations

  • Consultation and advocacy — running election campaigns, direct action, media and public education.
  • Charity and donations — giving financial aid to other organisations in support of democratic arrangements.
  • Legal aid — providing legal help to individuals and organisations.
  • Networking — establishing a system of contacts and exchange between people and organisations.
  • Policy — taking part in making the policies of the organisations' aims and methods.
  • Research — encouraging research on particular matters.
  • Technical support — giving consultation and technical help for solving problems.
  • Training — developing people's special knowledge and skills.

Their Role in Public Welfare

Civil society organisations create awareness among the people about their rights and problems. They work as a link between the government and the people, help poor and needy people, take part in education, health and other services, and press the government for solving public problems.

People join these organisations because of the spirit of serving their community and its welfare, the desire to protect rights, the desire to promote democracy and justice, and the desire to solve the problems of their area together.

Examples in Pakistan

OrganisationServices / Work
ScoutsTraining of youth, creating discipline and the spirit of service
Girl GuidesTraining of girls, self-confidence and service of the community
Youth Assembly in PakistanCreating awareness of democratic values, leadership and public problems among the youth

mcqs.q: A person who works for an organisation without any payment is called _______.
mcqs.why: A volunteer works for an organisation without payment of any compensation. Volunteers serve their community through civil society organisations.

mcqs.q: The basic role of a civil society organisation is to limit and regulate the authority of _______.
mcqs.why: The basic role of a civil society organisation is to limit and regulate the authority of the state. In this way it protects the rights of the citizens.

mcqs.q: A civil society organisation can provide a development field for future political _______.
mcqs.why: Civil society organisations give people training and experience of public work. In this way they can provide a development field for future political leaders.

mcqs.q: According to the book, volunteer activity plays an important role in progress in _______.
mcqs.why: The book's summary states that volunteer activity plays an important role in progress in the global economy. Volunteers give their time and skills free for the welfare of society.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a duty of civil society organisations?
options: Providing legal aid to individuals and organisations
mcqs.why: Providing legal help to individuals and organisations is one of the duties of civil society organisations. Their other duties include training, research, networking and advocacy.

mcqs.q: Civil society organisations work as a link between _______ and the people.
mcqs.why: Civil society organisations work as a link between the government and the people. They take public problems to the government and create awareness among the people.

mcqs.q: What is the work of the Scouts?
options: Training of youth, creating discipline and the spirit of service
mcqs.why: The Scouts do the training of youth and create discipline and the spirit of service in them. They are a well-known civil society organisation for young people.

mcqs.q: What do the Girl Guides do?
options: Training of girls, self-confidence and service of the community
mcqs.why: The Girl Guides work for the training of girls, building their self-confidence and serving the community. Like the Scouts, they promote volunteer activity.

mcqs.q: Why do people join civil society organisations?
options: Because of the spirit of serving their community and its welfare
mcqs.why: People join these organisations because of the spirit of serving their community and its welfare. They also want to protect rights and promote democracy and justice.

mcqs.q: Under 'charity and donations', civil society organisations _______.
options: Give financial aid to other organisations in support of democratic arrangements
mcqs.why: Under charity and donations, civil society organisations give financial aid to other organisations. This support is given for democratic arrangements and public welfare.

chapters.title: Unit 3: The Land of Asia and Its Life

lessons.title: The Land of Asia
lessons.notes_html:
Asia — The Largest Continent

The land area of Asia is 17,212,000 square miles. Its coastal area is about 62,800 kilometres long. Asia has great mountains, high plateaus and large deserts.

Mountains, Plateaus and Deserts of Asia

MountainsPlateausDeserts
Altai, Tien Shan, Ghats, Ural, Zagros, Kunlun, Karakoram, HimalayasIranian Plateau, Deccan Plateau, Tibetan PlateauGobi, Arabian, Thar, Karakum
  • Ural is a mountain range which lies in the northern area between Russia and Kazakhstan.
  • The Karakoram mountain range is situated in Pakistan and China.
  • The Arabian Peninsula is situated between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.

Important Terms

  • Plain and low-lying area: flat and low land, such as the plains along rivers and the low-lying areas along the sea (most of Bangladesh is like this).
  • Contour-line map: the map in which lines (contour lines) show the different heights of an area.
  • Summer monsoon: winds blowing from the sea towards the land in summer, which cause heavy rain.
  • Aerial photograph: a photograph taken from an aeroplane, which shows the shape of the land and buildings in greater detail.

How the Two Great Deserts Formed

The Gobi Desert is very far from the sea, so the sea winds cannot reach there; desert winds blow the sand about and the dryness increases every year. The Arabian Desert lies between the Equator and the Tropic of Cancer, where the sun's rays fall directly, so there is extreme heat; its small water stores cannot produce cool winds, so the land stays hot.

Living on the Coast: Britain or Bangladesh?

Bangladesh has heavy monsoon rains, floods and cyclones every year, and the rise in sea level causes great damage to its low-lying areas. Britain is also affected by the rise in sea level, but its damage is less than that of Bangladesh.

Desert Plants of Asia

Plants that survive in the deserts of Asia include the date palm tree, the cactus, and thorny bushes and grasses (such as lana and babul).

mcqs.q: What is the land area of Asia?
mcqs.why: The land area of Asia is 17,212,000 square miles. Asia is the largest continent of the world, with a coastline about 62,800 kilometres long.

mcqs.q: Ural is the name of a _______.
mcqs.why: Ural is the name of a mountain range. It lies in the northern area between Russia and Kazakhstan.

mcqs.q: The Arabian Peninsula is situated between _______ and the Persian Gulf.
mcqs.why: The Arabian Peninsula is situated between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf. It is the largest peninsula of Asia.

mcqs.q: In which countries is the Karakoram mountain range situated?
mcqs.why: The Karakoram mountain range is situated in Pakistan and China. It is one of the great mountain ranges of Asia, along with the Himalayas and Kunlun.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a plateau of Asia?
mcqs.why: The Tibetan Plateau is one of the plateaus of Asia, along with the Iranian and Deccan plateaus. Gobi, Thar and Karakum are deserts, not plateaus.

mcqs.q: A map in which lines show the different heights of an area is called a _______ map.
mcqs.why: A contour-line map uses lines, called contour lines, to show the different heights of an area. It helps us understand the shape and height of the land.

mcqs.q: Summer monsoon winds blow _______.
options: From the land towards the sea
From the sea towards the land, causing heavy rain
From north to south without rain
mcqs.why: Summer monsoon winds blow from the sea towards the land in summer. They carry moisture and cause heavy rain in South Asia.

mcqs.q: Why did the Gobi Desert form?
options: Because people cut all its trees
Because it is very far from the sea, so sea winds cannot reach there
mcqs.why: The Gobi Desert is very far from the sea, so moist sea winds cannot reach there. Desert winds blow the sand about and dryness increases every year.

mcqs.q: Why is the Arabian Desert extremely hot?
options: It lies between the Equator and the Tropic of Cancer, where the sun's rays fall directly
It is near the North Pole
mcqs.why: The Arabian Desert lies between the Equator and the Tropic of Cancer, where the sun's rays fall directly. Its small water stores cannot produce cool winds, so the land stays hot.

mcqs.q: Which of these plants is found in the deserts of Asia?
mcqs.why: The date palm tree grows in the deserts of Asia. Other desert plants are the cactus and thorny bushes and grasses such as lana and babul.

lessons.title: Interaction Between People and Countries
lessons.notes_html:
People and Countries of Asia

The two most populous countries of the world, China and India, are situated in Asia. The important agricultural crop of Bangladesh is rice. Borneo is situated in South-East Asia; its area is divided between Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei. The capital city of Malaysia is Kuala Lumpur.

Protecting the Forests

  • Stop the cutting of trees and plant new trees (tree plantation).
  • Make laws for the protection of forests and enforce them.
  • Protect against forest fires.
  • Use other material instead of wood.
  • Keep the habitats of animals safe.

Life in the Arabian Desert

The people living in the Arabian Desert rear camels, goats and sheep, and cultivate dates and other crops. The Bedouin tribes travel for fodder and trade in far-off areas. In the modern age, the discovery of oil, means of transport, work in urban areas and construction of buildings are also their important activities. The biggest natural source of water there is underground water; people take water from wells and oases and store it carefully.

Desalination

Desalination is a practical method of removing salt and minerals from salty water — the process of making salty water sweet. It is very useful in dry desert and coastal areas.

Climate Change and Asia

Because of climate change the sea level is rising, which has increased the danger of coastal areas sinking and of floods. In some places there is heavy rain and floods, while in others there is drought; deserts are expanding; crops are destroyed, there is a shortage of water, and people's health is badly affected. Low-lying countries like Bangladesh are affected the most.

People, Places and Environment

Physical featuresProfessionImportance for local peopleCauses of rain
DesertRearing animals and growing datesAnimals and dates provide livelihoodFar from the sea and dry winds, so rain is very scarce
ForestWood work and collecting forest produceWood, fruit and medicines are obtainedMany trees and humidity, so rain is plentiful
Coastal landFishing and tradeFish and employment from the seaMoist winds coming from the sea

mcqs.q: The two most populous countries of the world are China and _______.
mcqs.why: China and India, the two most populous countries of the world, are both situated in Asia. This is why Asia has more people than any other continent.

mcqs.q: The important agricultural crop of Bangladesh is _______.
mcqs.why: Rice is the important agricultural crop of Bangladesh. Its plains and heavy monsoon rains are very suitable for growing rice.

mcqs.q: Borneo is situated in which part of Asia?
mcqs.why: Borneo is situated in South-East Asia. Its area is divided between three countries: Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei.

mcqs.q: What is the capital city of Malaysia?
mcqs.why: Kuala Lumpur is the capital city of Malaysia. Malaysia is one of the countries of South-East Asia.

mcqs.q: Desalination is the process of _______.
options: Making salty water sweet by removing salt and minerals
mcqs.why: Desalination is a practical method of removing salt and minerals from salty water, making it sweet and usable. It is very useful in deserts and coastal areas.

mcqs.q: Which is a correct way to protect forests?
options: Planting new trees and enforcing forest-protection laws
mcqs.why: Forests can be protected by stopping tree cutting, planting new trees, and making and enforcing laws for their protection. Protecting animal habitats is also part of forest protection.

mcqs.q: What do the Bedouin tribes of the Arabian Desert mainly do?
options: They rear camels, goats and sheep and travel for fodder and trade
mcqs.why: The people of the Arabian Desert rear camels, goats and sheep and grow dates. The Bedouin tribes travel from place to place for fodder and trade.

mcqs.q: What is the biggest natural source of water in the Arabian Desert?
mcqs.why: According to the book, the biggest natural source of the Arabian Desert is underground water. People take water from wells and oases and use it carefully.

mcqs.q: Which country is affected the most by the rising sea level and climate change?
mcqs.why: Low-lying countries like Bangladesh are affected the most by climate change. Rising sea level increases the danger of coastal areas sinking and of floods there.

mcqs.q: In a forest area, why is rain plentiful?
options: Because the land is very high
Because there are many trees and humidity
mcqs.why: In forest areas there are many trees and much humidity, so rain is plentiful. In deserts, being far from the sea with dry winds, rain is very scarce.

lessons.title: Agricultural Water Uses and Effects
lessons.notes_html:
Key Terms

  • Evaporation: the process in which water changes into vapour.
  • Surface flow (surface runoff): the process in which water flows over the surface of the earth.
  • Irrigation: the means of supplying water to the land by human hands for the growth of plants and farming.
  • Weathering: a process of facing bad weather conditions in which rocks and minerals break up and scatter.

The three important sources of water in Pakistan are rain water, underground water and river water.

The Water Cycle

The water cycle is the system in which water is always in motion. With the heat of the sun, the water of seas, rivers and lakes becomes vapour and rises up. In the cold air above, the vapour becomes clouds. From the clouds, water falls on the land as rain or snow. Some water flows over the surface into rivers, some is absorbed into the land and becomes underground water, and in the end the water reaches back to the sea.

Floods: Causes and Protection

A flood occurs when water becomes too much on the land and cannot be contained in rivers or drains. Its causes are heavy rain, extra water coming into rivers, cutting of forests and increase in urban population. To reduce the intensity of floods: stop cutting forests and plant trees; repair and clean embankments and rivers; ban construction in flood areas by law; make a good drainage system for rain water; and give timely warning and safety preparation.

How People Make Water Dirty

People use water for drinking, bathing, washing clothes, irrigation, industry, making electricity and recreation. Water becomes dirty when dirty water from homes, factory waste, rubbish, chemical substances and animal waste are thrown into rivers, lakes and seas. This is called water pollution.

Erosion, Transportation and Deposition

  • Erosion: water, wind or ice breaks rock and land and carries it from one place to another.
  • Transportation: carrying broken rock and soil from one place to another through water or wind.
  • Deposition: when the flow of water becomes slow, the carried material collects at another place — for example, soil collecting at the bank of a river and forming a delta.

The Three Courses of a River

Upper courseMiddle courseLower course
In high mountain areas; water flows fast; the valley is narrow and V-shaped; waterfalls formThe flow becomes gentle; the valley becomes wide; flood plains and bends of the river form; soil starts collectingThe flow becomes very slow; the river becomes wide and deep; much soil collects; deltas and lakes form

mcqs.q: The process in which water changes into vapour is called _______.
mcqs.why: Evaporation is the process in which water changes into vapour due to the heat of the sun. It is the first step of the water cycle.

mcqs.q: Water flowing over the surface of the earth is known as _______.
mcqs.why: The process in which water flows over the surface of the earth is known as surface flow or surface runoff. Some of this water joins rivers and finally reaches the sea.

mcqs.q: The three important sources of water in Pakistan are rain water, river water and _______.
mcqs.why: The three important sources of water in Pakistan are rain water, underground water and river water. Underground water is taken out through wells and tube wells.

mcqs.q: Irrigation means _______.
options: Supplying water to the land by human hands for the growth of plants and farming
mcqs.why: Irrigation is the means of supplying water to the land by human hands for the growth of plants and farming. Canals, wells and tube wells are used for irrigation.

mcqs.q: In weathering, _______ break up and scatter due to bad weather conditions.
mcqs.why: Weathering is the process in which rocks and minerals break up and scatter when they face bad weather conditions. It slowly changes the surface of the land.

mcqs.q: In the water cycle, water vapour in the cold air above becomes _______.
mcqs.why: In the water cycle, vapour rises and becomes clouds in the cold air above. From the clouds, water falls back on the land as rain or snow.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a cause of floods?
options: Heavy rain and cutting of forests
mcqs.why: Floods are caused by heavy rain, extra water coming into rivers, cutting of forests and increase in urban population. Planting trees and cleaning rivers help to reduce floods.

mcqs.q: Throwing factory waste, rubbish and chemicals into rivers and seas is called _______.
mcqs.why: When dirty water from homes, factory waste, rubbish, chemicals and animal waste are thrown into rivers, lakes and seas, it is called water pollution. It makes water harmful for people, animals and plants.

mcqs.q: When the flow of water becomes slow and the carried material collects at another place, the process is called _______.
mcqs.why: Deposition happens when the flow of water becomes slow and the carried soil and rock collect at another place. Soil collecting at the bank of a river and forming a delta is an example.

mcqs.q: In the upper course of a river, the valley is _______.
mcqs.why: In the upper course, in high mountain areas, water flows fast and the valley is narrow and V-shaped, and waterfalls form. In the lower course the river becomes wide and slow and forms deltas.

lessons.title: People on the Move — Migration and Settlements
lessons.notes_html:
Voluntary and Forced Migration

In voluntary migration, people move from one place to another of their own will — for example, for better employment, education or a better standard of living. In forced migration, people leave home under compulsion — for example, because of war, natural disaster, oppression or pressure from the government.

Who is a Refugee?

Forced migration is the process in which people leave their home under compulsion, inside the country or outside it. A refugee is that person who leaves his own country because of war, oppression or fear and takes shelter in another country. Remember: every refugee is a forced migrant, but every forced migrant is not a refugee — some people become homeless inside their own country.

Why Do Refugees Leave Their Homes?

  • War and fighting become a danger to their lives.
  • They face oppression and fear because of their race, religion or political views.
  • The government or armed groups force them to leave home.
  • Sometimes natural disasters (floods, drought) also force them to leave home.

Examples: the migration between Pakistan and India in 1947, and the migration of millions of people to Pakistan and Iran because of the war in Afghanistan.

Push and Pull Factors

When we study a migrant's story, we separate the push factors (poverty, war, disaster — things that force a person to leave) from the pull factors (jobs and facilities — things that attract a person to the new place).

Urbanisation and Growth Poles

  • Urbanisation is the change from village life towards city life.
  • A growth pole is a single urban centre which attracts people, resources and wealth towards itself.
  • In East Asia, population is found in river valleys and coastal plains.

Settlements and Their Facilities

SettlementExampleFacilities provided
CityKarachiSchools, hospitals, electricity, water, roads, market, seaport
TownsHyderabad, SukkurSchools, hospital, electricity, water, bazaar, roads
VillagesVillages of one's own talukaPrimary school, mosque, well/water, roads, agricultural land

mcqs.q: In voluntary migration, people move _______.
options: Of their own will, for better employment, education or a better standard of living
mcqs.why: In voluntary migration people move of their own will, for example for better employment, education or a better standard of living. In forced migration people leave under compulsion.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of forced migration?
options: Leaving home because of war or oppression
Going to a city for a better job
mcqs.why: Leaving home because of war, natural disaster, oppression or government pressure is forced migration. People do not leave by choice but under compulsion.

mcqs.q: A refugee is a person who _______.
options: Leaves his own country because of war, oppression or fear and takes shelter in another country
Works in another city for some months
mcqs.why: A refugee leaves his own country because of war, oppression or fear and takes shelter in another country. Every refugee is a forced migrant, but not every forced migrant is a refugee.

mcqs.q: Why are some forced migrants NOT refugees?
options: Because some people become homeless inside their own country
mcqs.why: Forced migration can happen inside a country or outside it. A person who is forced to leave home but stays inside his own country is a forced migrant, not a refugee.

mcqs.q: Which of these forces refugees to leave their homes?
options: Oppression and fear because of race, religion or political views
mcqs.why: Refugees leave because war endangers their lives, or they face oppression and fear because of their race, religion or political views. Armed groups and governments may also force them out.

mcqs.q: The migration between Pakistan and India in 1947 is an example of _______.
mcqs.why: In 1947 millions of people were forced to leave their homes between Pakistan and India. The war in Afghanistan also forced millions to migrate to Pakistan and Iran.

mcqs.q: The change from village life towards city life is called _______.
mcqs.why: Urbanisation is the change from village life towards city life. As cities grow, more and more people leave villages and settle in urban areas.

mcqs.q: A single urban centre which attracts people, resources and wealth towards itself is called a _______.
mcqs.why: A growth pole is a single urban centre which attracts people, resources and wealth towards itself. Karachi is an example of such a centre in Sindh.

mcqs.q: In East Asia, population is mostly found in _______.
mcqs.why: In East Asia, population is found in river valleys and coastal plains. These areas have water, fertile land and facilities, so people settle there in large numbers.

mcqs.q: Jobs and facilities at a new place are examples of _______ factors of migration.
mcqs.why: Pull factors attract a person to a new place, such as jobs and facilities. Push factors, such as poverty, war and disaster, force a person to leave the old place.

lessons.title: Demand (Consumer-Focused View)
lessons.notes_html:
What is Demand?

Consumer demand describes a consumer's desire to buy a particular good or service at a particular price, together with the ability to pay for it and the intention to pay. Examples: Asif buying a pen for 10 rupees; a household's demand for sugar; students' demand for books.

The two basic types of demand are individual demand and market demand.

The Law of Demand

When the price of a good increases, the quantity demanded decreases. When the price falls, the quantity demanded rises. A list of prices and quantities demanded is a demand schedule, and its diagrammatic presentation is called the demand curve. The demand curve slopes down from left to right.

Price of biscuits (Rs.)7654321
Quantity demanded (packets)1247111623

Income

Income is the amount of money a person receives on a regular basis as payment for their work. Examples: the wage a factory worker receives at the end of the month; a shopkeeper's profit; a farmer's money from selling the crop.

Complementary Goods

Complementary goods are goods that are used together with each other. When the price of one good falls, the demand for its complementary good also increases. Example: if the price of tea falls, people buy more tea, and the demand for sugar also rises — even though the price of sugar has not changed.

GoodComplementary goodSubstitute good
TeaSugar, milkCoffee
Mobile phoneSIM, chargerLandline phone
PenInk, copyPencil
CarPetrolMotorcycle, bus
ShoeSocks, polishSlippers

Substitute Goods

Substitute goods are goods that consumers can use in place of each other for the same purpose. When the price of one good rises, the demand for its substitute increases. Example: if the price of butter rises, people buy margarine instead; if the price of tea rises, the demand for coffee rises.

Non-Price Factors That Affect Demand

  • Change in population
  • Change in tastes and preferences
  • Change in income
  • Change in the price of substitute goods
  • Season and weather conditions
  • Expected price and fear of shortage
  • Change in fashion

Fear of shortage: if a shortage of a good is expected in the near future, people buy more of it in advance, so its quantity demanded increases even at a high price.

mcqs.q: When the price of a good increases, the quantity demanded _______.
mcqs.why: According to the law of demand, when the price increases the quantity demanded decreases. When the price falls, the quantity demanded rises.

mcqs.q: The two basic types of demand are _______ and market demand.
mcqs.why: The two basic types of demand are individual demand and market demand. Individual demand is of one consumer; market demand is of all consumers together.

mcqs.q: The diagrammatic presentation of a demand schedule is called _______.
mcqs.why: The diagrammatic presentation of a demand schedule is called the demand curve. It slopes down from left to right, showing that quantity demanded rises as price falls.

mcqs.q: Consumer demand means desire to buy a good together with _______.
options: Ability to pay and intention to pay
mcqs.why: Consumer demand is a consumer's desire to buy a good or service at a particular price, together with the ability to pay for it and the intention to pay. Desire alone is not demand.

mcqs.q: Income is _______.
options: The amount of money a person receives regularly as payment for work
mcqs.why: Income is the amount of money a person receives on a regular basis as payment for their work. Examples are a factory worker's monthly wage and a farmer's money from selling the crop.

mcqs.q: Complementary goods are goods that are _______.
options: Used in place of each other
mcqs.why: Complementary goods are used together, like tea and sugar, or a car and petrol. One good is needed along with the other.

mcqs.q: If the price of tea falls, what happens to the demand for sugar?
mcqs.why: Sugar is a complementary good of tea. When the price of tea falls, people buy more tea, so the demand for sugar also rises, even though the price of sugar has not changed.

mcqs.q: Substitute goods are goods that _______.
options: Consumers can use in place of each other for the same purpose
mcqs.why: Substitute goods can be used in place of each other for the same purpose, like tea and coffee, or butter and margarine. Consumers switch to the cheaper one.

mcqs.q: If the price of butter rises, the demand for margarine will _______.
mcqs.why: Margarine is a substitute for butter. When the price of butter rises, people buy margarine instead because it is cheaper, so the demand for margarine increases.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a non-price factor that affects demand?
mcqs.why: Change in population is a non-price factor that affects demand. Other non-price factors are changes in income, tastes and preferences, season and weather, and expected prices.

mcqs.q: Manzha bought coffee instead of tea because the price of coffee had fallen. This is because tea and coffee are _______ goods.
mcqs.why: Tea and coffee are substitute goods. When the price of coffee fell, Manzha switched to the cheaper item and increased her demand for coffee instead of tea.

mcqs.q: Asad hears that a shortage of powdered milk is expected soon. What will happen to his quantity demanded?
options: It will increase, because of fear of shortage
mcqs.why: Because of the fear of shortage, Asad will buy more milk in advance, so his quantity demanded will increase. Expected shortage raises demand even when the price is high.

mcqs.q: The demand curve slopes _______.
mcqs.why: The demand curve slopes down from left to right. This shape shows the law of demand: as the price falls, the quantity demanded rises.

mcqs.q: In the biscuit demand schedule, at a price of Rs. 5 the quantity demanded is _______ packets.
mcqs.why: In the demand schedule, at Rs. 7 one packet is demanded, at Rs. 6 two packets, and at Rs. 5 four packets are demanded. As the price falls to Re. 1, the quantity rises to 23 packets.

mcqs.q: Which of these pairs is a pair of complementary goods?
mcqs.why: A car and petrol are complementary goods because they are used together — a car does not run without petrol. Tea and coffee, and butter and margarine, are substitutes.

lessons.title: Supply (Producer-Focused View)
lessons.notes_html:
Who is a Producer?

The person who produces economic value or goods and services is called a producer. A producer produces and provides goods or services and sells them to consumers, governments or other firms. Examples: a farmer growing wheat; a factory making cloth; a firm making shoes. The government is also a producer of services, such as police, defence and government schools.

Supply and the Law of Supply

Supply describes the total quantity of a particular good or service that is available to consumers. When the price of a good rises, producers offer a larger quantity; when the price falls, supply also falls, because at a lower price the profit is also less. A supply schedule presents the relation between the price of a good or service and the quantity supplied through a schedule, and the supply curve drawn from it slopes upwards from left to right.

Price of DVD (Rs.)50100150200250
Quantity supplied1591317

Incentive

An incentive is something that moves a person to perform an action or encourages them. In economics it is a payment or concession for greater production or investment. Examples: awards given to employees, bonuses, increase in salary, certificates and praise. A punishment used to discourage an activity is a negative incentive.

Revenue and Profit

  • Revenue = unit price × quantity sold.
  • Profit is the reward a producer gets for taking a risk. It is obtained when the revenue from selling the production exceeds the total cost.
  • Total profit = Total revenue − Total expenses. Revenue is the total income; profit is the amount left after deducting expenses.

Non-Price Factors That Affect Supply

  • Cost of production / production expenses
  • Price of related goods
  • Productive capacity
  • Technology — if there is progress in the technology of production, supply increases
  • The seller's expectations about future prices
  • Weather and natural disasters, taxes and subsidy, strikes, and availability of transport and electricity

Conditions of the Law of Supply

The relation "higher price, more supply" holds when other things remain the same: there is no change in the price of related goods, no change in the factors of production, no change in technology, no change in government policy, and no change in the seller's expectations about future prices.

mcqs.q: The person who produces economic value or goods and services is called _______.
mcqs.why: A producer is the person who produces and provides goods or services and sells them to consumers, governments or other firms. A farmer growing wheat and a factory making cloth are producers.

mcqs.q: If there is progress in the technology of production of a good, its supply will _______.
mcqs.why: Progress in the technology of production increases supply. Better technology lets producers make more goods at a lower cost.

mcqs.q: A _______ presents the relation between the price of a good and the quantity supplied through a schedule.
mcqs.why: A supply schedule presents the relation between the price of a good or service and the quantity supplied for the stated time. The supply curve is drawn from this schedule.

mcqs.q: When the price of a good falls, its supply _______.
options: Also falls, because profit is less
mcqs.why: When the price falls, supply also falls, because producers offer a smaller quantity at a lower price where the profit is also less. This is the law of supply.

mcqs.q: Revenue is equal to _______.
mcqs.why: Revenue = unit price × quantity sold. Revenue is the total income from selling the goods, before expenses are deducted.

mcqs.q: Total profit is equal to _______.
mcqs.why: Total profit = Total revenue − Total expenses. Profit is the amount left after deducting all expenses from the total income.

mcqs.q: Profit is the reward a producer gets for _______.
mcqs.why: Profit is the reward a producer gets for taking a risk. It is obtained when the revenue from selling the production exceeds the total cost of the goods or services.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an incentive?
mcqs.why: An incentive is something that encourages a person to act, such as awards, bonuses, increase in salary, certificates and praise. A punishment is a negative incentive used to discourage an activity.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a non-price factor that affects supply?
mcqs.why: Cost of production is a non-price factor that affects supply. Other such factors are the price of related goods, productive capacity, technology and the seller's expectations.

mcqs.q: The law of supply holds when other things remain the same, for example there is no change in _______.
mcqs.why: The price–supply relation holds when there is no change in technology, in the price of related goods, in the factors of production, in government policy or in the seller's expectations.

mcqs.q: In the DVD supply schedule, at a price of Rs. 250 the quantity supplied is _______.
mcqs.why: In the supply schedule, at Rs. 50 the quantity supplied is 1, and it rises with the price to 17 at Rs. 250. This shows the direct relation between price and supply.

mcqs.q: The supply curve slopes _______.
mcqs.why: The supply curve rises upwards from left to right. This shape shows that as the price rises, the quantity supplied also rises.

mcqs.q: The government is also a producer of services, such as _______.
mcqs.why: The government produces services like police, defence and government schools. Producers can be farmers, factories, firms or the government.

mcqs.q: If taxes on production rise, what will happen to supply?
options: It will decrease, because production becomes costly
mcqs.why: A rise in tax makes production costly, so supply decreases. On the other hand, a subsidy (government help) lowers cost and increases supply.

mcqs.q: A punishment given to discourage a particular activity is called a _______ incentive.
mcqs.why: A negative incentive, such as a punishment, discourages a particular activity. A positive incentive, such as a reward or praise, encourages an activity.

chapters.title: Unit 5: Organisation of the People in Asia

lessons.title: Gaining Group Leadership and Practical Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Leaders and Followers

People are naturally divided into leaders and followers. A leader guides the group, makes plans and takes the group towards its destination.

Ways of Becoming a Leader

  • Heredity — leadership passes in a family from one generation to another.
  • Power — a person gains leadership by using power (force).
  • Appointment — a leader is appointed for a particular purpose.
  • Elections — the people choose a leader through votes.
  • Voluntary action — people guide others of their own will for the good of others.

Three Styles of Leadership

StyleHow the leader worksEffect on the group
Absolute leaderMakes decisions according to his own choice, without the advice of people, and keeps complete authority with himselfMembers cannot express their ideas
Democratic leaderParticipates in decision-making and also includes others; encourages them and gets them to express their ideasMembers cooperate and obey willingly
Leader who gives freedomGives people the freedom to work according to their own choice, with the least interferenceMembers work freely in their own way

How Leaders Prevent Differences in Groups

  • Remain silent and show respect — look at others' point of view with honour and respect.
  • Enforce reasonableness and reach agreement — clarify the facts and bring the groups to a conclusion.
  • Think creatively and use authority — search for a better solution to the problem and use authority when needed.

Other ways are: listen to both sides separately, make peace through a mediator, make common rules on which everyone agrees, encourage admitting mistakes and asking for forgiveness, and increase friendship through joint games or joint work.

If There Were No Leader

If there were no leader in a society, no decision would be taken, everyone would do as they pleased, quarrels would increase and work would stop. A class monitor, for example, keeps discipline in the class, manages the class in the teacher's absence, conveys the students' problems to the teacher and teaches everyone to work together.

mcqs.q: A democratic leader is a leader who _______.
options: Participates in decision-making and includes others in decisions
mcqs.why: A democratic leader plays an active role in decision-making and also includes others in decisions. He encourages the members and gets them to express their ideas.

mcqs.q: Absolute leaders make decisions _______.
options: According to their own choice, without the advice of people
With the help of a mediator
mcqs.why: An absolute leader makes decisions according to his own choice without the advice of people. He keeps complete authority with himself, unlike a democratic leader.

mcqs.q: People are naturally divided into _______ and followers.
mcqs.why: People are naturally divided into leaders and followers. Leaders guide the group, while followers work under their guidance.

mcqs.q: When the people choose a leader through votes, this way of becoming a leader is called _______.
mcqs.why: In elections, the people choose a leader through votes. In heredity, leadership passes in a family from one generation to another.

mcqs.q: Leadership passing in a family from one generation to another is called _______.
mcqs.why: Heredity means leadership passes in a family from one generation to another. It is one of the five ways through which people can become leaders.

mcqs.q: A leader is appointed for a particular purpose in which way?
mcqs.why: In appointment, a leader is appointed for a particular purpose. A class monitor chosen by the teacher for the class is an example.

mcqs.q: To prevent differences, a leader should first _______.
options: Remain silent and show respect to others' point of view
mcqs.why: The first method of the book is to remain silent and show honour and respect, looking at others' point of view with respect. Then facts are clarified and the groups are brought to an agreement.

mcqs.q: Making peace through a third person is called peace through a _______.
mcqs.why: A mediator is a neutral person who helps two sides make peace. Leaders can also listen to both sides separately and make common rules to remove differences.

mcqs.q: What happens in a society if there is no leader?
options: No decision is taken, quarrels increase and work stops
mcqs.why: Without a leader, no decision would be taken and everyone would do as they pleased. Quarrels would increase and the work of society would stop.

mcqs.q: What is one benefit of having a monitor in the class?
options: He keeps discipline and conveys students' problems to the teacher
mcqs.why: A class monitor keeps discipline in the class and manages it in the teacher's absence. He also conveys the students' problems to the teacher and teaches everyone to work together.

lessons.title: Organised Speech of Asian Peoples and Response to Crises
lessons.notes_html:
Women and Youth in Society

Women have a role to play in every society as a nation builder. Countries are producing educated youth in large numbers, but they lack basic skills and practical training.

The Problem-Solving Cycle

Groups and individual people work together to cope with difficulties through the problem-solving cycle:

  • Step 1 — Identifying: recognising the problem.
  • Step 2 — Gathering information and creating ideas.
  • Step 3 — Selecting the best idea.
  • Step 4 — Strengthening and testing the idea.
  • Step 5 — Evaluating the results and determining their value.

In addition, groups, the government and civil organisations work together and help one another.

Ending the Shortage of Water and Cutting of Forests

  • For the shortage of water: building dams and reservoirs, saving water, telling people about the proper use of water, and keeping rivers and seas clean.
  • For the cutting of forests: protecting trees, planting trees, informing people about the importance of trees, and cooperating with the government in this work. People cut trees to obtain land and to provide residential facilities for the people — this destruction must be stopped.

The Five Regions of Asia

RegionExample countries
South-East AsiaIndonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines
South AsiaPakistan, India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Afghanistan, Bhutan, Maldives
West AsiaSaudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, Turkey, Syria, Jordan
Central AsiaKazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan
East AsiaChina, Japan, Korea, Mongolia

Reform Suggestions for the Energy Crisis

Saving electricity and stopping its wastage; using new sources of electricity (solar energy, wind energy); stopping electricity theft; energy-saving habits in industry and homes; and the government and the people working together.

Who Deals with a Crisis?

CrisisGroup dealing with it
Shortage of water in schoolSchool administration and municipal body
Rubbish and diseases in the streetCleaning staff and health department
Load-shedding of electricityElectricity company
Quarrels in schoolTeachers and parents

mcqs.q: Women have a role to play in every society as a _______.
mcqs.why: Women have a role to play in every society as a nation builder. Their work in the family, education and society builds the nation.

mcqs.q: Educated youth are produced in large numbers, but they lack basic skills and _______.
mcqs.why: Countries are producing educated youth in large numbers, but they lack basic skills and practical training. Practical training is needed along with book education.

mcqs.q: What is the first step of the problem-solving cycle?
mcqs.why: The first step of the problem-solving cycle is identifying, that is, recognising the problem. Only after recognising the problem can information be gathered and ideas created.

mcqs.q: In the problem-solving cycle, after gathering information and creating ideas, we _______.
mcqs.why: The third step of the cycle is selecting the best idea from the ideas created. Then the idea is strengthened and tested, and finally the results are evaluated.

mcqs.q: Which step comes last in the problem-solving cycle?
options: Evaluating the results and determining their value
mcqs.why: Evaluating the results and determining their value is the fifth and last step of the problem-solving cycle. It tells us whether the solution worked or not.

mcqs.q: People start cutting trees and destroying forests in order to _______.
options: Obtain land and provide residential facilities for the people
mcqs.why: People cut trees and destroy forests to obtain land and to provide residential facilities for the people. This causes shortage of trees and harms the environment.

mcqs.q: Which of these can end the shortage of water?
options: Building dams and reservoirs and saving water
mcqs.why: The shortage of water can be ended by building dams and reservoirs, saving water and telling people about its proper use. Keeping rivers and seas clean also helps.

mcqs.q: Which country belongs to Central Asia?
mcqs.why: Kazakhstan is a country of Central Asia, along with Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. Pakistan is in South Asia and Japan in East Asia.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a reform suggestion for the energy crisis?
options: Using new sources like solar and wind energy
mcqs.why: Using new sources of electricity, such as solar energy and wind energy, is a reform suggestion for the energy crisis. Saving electricity and stopping its theft and wastage also help.

mcqs.q: The crisis of rubbish and diseases in the street is dealt with by _______.
options: The cleaning staff and health department
mcqs.why: Rubbish and diseases in the street are dealt with by the cleaning staff and the health department. Every crisis has a responsible group; for load-shedding it is the electricity company.

lessons.title: Organisation of Asian Society: Rights and Responsibilities
lessons.notes_html:
Rights at Different Ages

GroupRightsResponsibilities
ChildrenEducation, protection, health, playing and receiving loveStudying, obeying parents and teachers, following the rules of the school
AdultsVoting (at the age of 18), employment, expressing their own opinionFollowing the law, serving the country, respecting the rights of others
Elderly citizensRespect, care and protectionGuiding the youth

According to the international standard, a person whose age is 18 years has the right to cast his vote in elections. When a child reaches the required age for going to school, he can exercise the right to education.

How Rights Are Implemented in Society

Rights are implemented when people know about their rights and responsibilities, respect them and follow the law. The government and the organisations of civil society work together and make such policies that girls too, like boys, can get basic education without any discrimination. Every citizen should become aware of their rights, respect the rights of others and work for the betterment of the country.

Factors That Shape Responsibilities

  • Economic factors — for example, supporting the family by working honestly.
  • Cultural factors — respect for one's own culture, festivals and traditions.
  • Factors related to age and status — respect for elders and care of the younger ones.
  • Religious factors — worship and truthfulness.

Groups in Society

In a society, a minority can be on the basis of nation, religion and race. Political parties identify the interests of the people, express them again and again, and present their manifesto in their context.

GroupWhat do they want in society?
Social groupBetterment of their area
Groups with common interestsThe interests of their members
Political partiesThe authority of government and implementing their manifesto
Minority groupEqual rights and protection
Community groupThe identity and interest of their community

Why Do Views Differ?

People of Asian society are organised in different groups and have their own ideas, interests and aims, with clear cultural differences in language, dress, traditions and ethics. When individuals and groups put their own individual aims ahead of the collective aims of society, problems like intolerance, bribery, unbalanced economy and child labour arise in society.

mcqs.q: According to the international standard, a person has the right to vote at the age of _______ years.
mcqs.why: According to the international standard, a person whose age is 18 years has the right to cast his vote in elections. Voting is a right of adult citizens.

mcqs.q: When a child reaches the required age for going to school, he can exercise the right of _______.
mcqs.why: When a child reaches school age, he can exercise the right to education. Children also have the rights of protection, health, playing and receiving love.

mcqs.q: In a society, a minority can be on the basis of nation, religion and _______.
mcqs.why: A minority in a society can be on the basis of nation, religion and race (ethnic basis). Minority groups want equal rights and protection.

mcqs.q: Political parties identify the _______ of the people and present their manifesto in their context.
mcqs.why: Political parties identify the interests of the people, express them again and again, and present their manifesto in their context. They seek the authority of government through elections.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a responsibility of children?
options: Studying and obeying parents and teachers
mcqs.why: The responsibilities of children are studying, obeying parents and teachers, and following the rules of the school. Voting and working are the rights and responsibilities of adults.

mcqs.q: What is the special right of elderly citizens?
mcqs.why: Elderly citizens have the rights of honour and respect, family care and support, health facilities and economic protection such as a pension. In return, they guide the youth from their experience.

mcqs.q: Rights are implemented in society when _______.
options: People know their rights and responsibilities, respect them and follow the law
mcqs.why: Rights are implemented when people know about their rights and responsibilities, respect them and follow the law. The government and civil society organisations also work together for this.

mcqs.q: Which of these factors shapes the responsibilities of people?
options: Economic, cultural, age-and-status and religious factors
mcqs.why: Four factors shape responsibilities: economic factors, cultural factors, factors related to age and status, and religious factors. They determine what a person's responsibility will be and how he fulfils it.

mcqs.q: What do minority groups want in society?
mcqs.why: Minority groups want equal rights and protection in society. They should be organised through equal rights and respect, without discrimination.

mcqs.q: When individuals put their own aims ahead of the collective aims of society, which problems arise?
options: Intolerance, bribery, unbalanced economy and child labour
mcqs.why: When individual aims are put ahead of collective aims, problems like intolerance, bribery, unbalanced economy and child labour arise in society. These problems harm the whole society.

lessons.title: Support Skills
lessons.notes_html:
Learning Together: Support Skills

Support skills are the special methods by which students learn together — cooperating with one another, asking questions, sharing material and respecting each other's opinions. In this chapter we examine classroom scenarios and judge whether they show good learning or not.

Two Classroom Scenarios
