  • Scenario 1: In the activity given by the doctor (teacher), students ask each other questions and give answers. This shows shared learning and cooperation — a suitable learning situation.
  • Scenario 2: Five students sit around a table preparing for the history exam, sharing the book, notes and mobile pictures. This shows group study and the use of technology.

While judging a scenario we give reasons: was the choice made because of the proposed activity, the technology, or the teacher's role?

Making an Unsuitable Scenario Suitable

If a scenario is unsuitable — for example because of lack of cooperation among students or wrong use of technology — we ask: what change is needed? For example, every student taking part and guidance by the teacher. The teacher and students together can bring that change, and such a change is desirable.

The Four-Box Sketch

BoxWhat to write
ResourcesBook, notes, mobile/tablet, board
PeopleStudents, teacher, group leader
ActivitiesAsking questions, discussion, sharing notes
ProcessWorking together, listening to each other, respecting opinions

To make a good scenario a reality in our own class we decide: which new resources are needed (study material and digital technology), which new roles need to be implemented (the active role of every student and guidance by the teacher), and the important changes in our activity (participation of all and punctuality).

mcqs.q: In the scenario activity of this chapter, each scenario is placed in the _______ column.
mcqs.why: Students read both scenarios carefully and place them in the 'suitable' or 'unsuitable' column. They also write where each scenario took place and give reasons for their choice.

mcqs.q: The first scenario — students asking each other questions and giving answers in the teacher's activity — shows _______.
mcqs.why: The first scenario shows shared learning and cooperation, because the students learn by asking each other questions and giving answers. Such a scenario is placed in the suitable column.

mcqs.q: The second scenario — five students preparing for the history exam by sharing the book, notes and mobile pictures — shows _______.
options: Group study and use of technology
mcqs.why: The second scenario shows group study and the use of technology. The students share the book, notes and mobile pictures to prepare together for the history exam.

mcqs.q: Which three things are considered while giving reasons for choosing a scenario?
options: The proposed activity, technology and the teacher's role
mcqs.why: While choosing a column for a scenario, reasons are given keeping in view the proposed activity, the technology used, or the teacher's role. These three things decide whether the learning situation is suitable.

mcqs.q: The four boxes of the sketch in this chapter are Resources, People, Activities and _______.
mcqs.why: The four boxes of the sketch are Resources, People, Activities and Process. For each scenario, the records are written in these four boxes.

mcqs.q: In the four-box sketch, a book, notes, mobile/tablet and board are written under _______.
mcqs.why: Book, notes, mobile/tablet and board are learning materials, so they are written under Resources. Students, teacher and group leader come under People.

mcqs.q: Working together, listening to each other and respecting opinions are written under which box?
mcqs.why: Working together, listening to each other and respecting opinions describe how the work is done, so they come under Process. Asking questions and discussion come under Activities.

mcqs.q: Who can bring the change needed to make an unsuitable scenario suitable?
mcqs.why: The teacher and students together can bring the change — for example, every student taking part and the teacher giving guidance. Such a change is desirable for better learning.

mcqs.q: Which new resources are needed to make a good scenario a reality in the class?
mcqs.why: The new resources needed are study material and digital technology. Along with this, the active role of every student and the guidance of the teacher are the new roles to be implemented.

mcqs.q: Which is an important change needed in our activity?
options: Participation of all students and punctuality
mcqs.why: Participation of all and punctuality are the important changes in our activity. When every student takes part and work is done on time, the learning scenario becomes a reality.

lessons.title: Problem-Solving and Decision-Making Skills
lessons.notes_html:
Solving the Problem of Poverty

Who is responsible for solving the problem of poverty? Government institutions (through policies and jobs), community organisations (through help and training) and the poor people themselves (through hard work and learning) — everyone has their own role.

An assumption can be presented like this: "The most effective solution to the problem of poverty is that poor people get education and training so that they can help themselves." Arguments are then given for and against the assumption.

Three Committees, Three Solutions

CommitteeWhat it investigates
First committeeHow poor people can improve their condition through education and re-training programmes
Second committeeWhat volunteer groups (religious organisations, non-government organisations and business organisations) can do through charity or better employment opportunities
Third committeeThe existing government poverty-eradication programmes and new proposals, including legislation about civil rights

Each committee presents its research report, and the class decides which solution is the most practicable and test-worthy. Information can also be collected by taking interviews from people of the neighbourhood or by writing letters; the whole project can be completed in one or two weeks.

The Egg-Protection Envelope: A Decision-Making Activity

  • Work in groups of 4 to 6 members and make an envelope that protects an egg.
  • Collect material: drinking straws, cardboard, tube, small bamboo sticks, sticking tape, glue, etc.
  • Use only four of the collected resources — the group decides which four, and decides the role of two members.
  • The egg must not break, but it will be dropped from at least eight feet above the ground.
  • Decisions are made by consensus or voting.

At the end the group discusses: What was our decision? How did we reach it? Which method of decision-making did we use? Who provided guidance? How were displeasures and contradictions controlled? How satisfied are we with our participation? The results are shown on a chart on the class bulletin board.

mcqs.q: According to this chapter, who is responsible for solving the problem of poverty?
options: Government institutions, community organisations and the poor people themselves
mcqs.why: Government institutions, community organisations and the poor people themselves are all included in solving poverty. Each has its own role: policies and jobs, help and training, and hard work and learning.

mcqs.q: The first sub-committee studies how poor people can improve their condition through _______.
mcqs.why: The first committee investigates education and re-training programmes for poor people. The second studies volunteer groups, and the third studies government programmes and civil-rights legislation.

mcqs.q: The second sub-committee investigates what _______ can do through charity or better employment opportunities.
options: Volunteer groups — religious, non-government and business organisations
mcqs.why: The second committee investigates volunteer groups, including religious organisations, non-government organisations and business organisations. Their help is given through charity or better employment opportunities.

mcqs.q: An assumption is _______.
options: A suggested idea presented with arguments for and against it
A final decision of the class
mcqs.why: An assumption is a suggested idea, for example: 'the most effective solution to poverty is that poor people get education and training so they can help themselves.' Arguments are given for and against it in the class.

mcqs.q: How is information about the community's problems collected in this project?
options: By taking interviews from people of the neighbourhood or writing letters
mcqs.why: Material is collected by taking interviews from people related to the neighbourhood or by writing letters. The whole project can be completed in one or two weeks.

mcqs.q: For the egg-protection envelope activity, each group has _______ members.
options: The whole class in one group
mcqs.why: The egg-protection envelope is made in groups of 4 to 6 members. Working in a group, students practise problem-solving and decision-making together.

mcqs.q: How many of the collected resources may be used to make the egg-protection envelope?
mcqs.why: Only four of the collected resources may be used. The group must decide by consensus or vote which four resources to use — this is the decision-making part of the activity.

mcqs.q: The egg-protection envelope is tested by dropping it from at least _______ above the ground.
mcqs.why: The envelope is dropped from at least eight feet above the ground. The envelope should be so strong and soft that the egg does not break.

mcqs.q: Which materials can be used for the egg-protection envelope?
options: Drinking straws, cardboard, tube, bamboo sticks, sticking tape and glue
mcqs.why: Drinking straws, cardboard, tube, small bamboo sticks, sticking tape and glue can be used for the envelope. The group selects only four of the collected resources.

mcqs.q: Which methods of decision-making are discussed at the end of the activity?
mcqs.why: At the end, groups discuss which method of decision-making they used — consensus (agreement of all) or voting. They also discuss who guided them and how differences were controlled.

lessons.title: History Skills
lessons.notes_html:
How Historians Study a Historical Site

Historians judge information on the basis of the greatest amount of collected information. When a historical site is excavated, pictures of the changes occurring in the land and of the pre-historical or remaining industrial samples are taken. After making the samples, they are kept with informative titles from which it appears where they were received. These steps ensure that a historian can tell where a sample was received and how those samples are related to each other.

One Sample Gives Only a Clue

From a single thing — for example a pencil — only a clue about its owner can be obtained; much cannot be told with certainty. But when many things are found together, more things can be understood from them. In the same way, historians estimate less from one sample and more from many samples received together.

The Bag Exercise

In the class exercise, every student shows the things in their bag, and the others guess who the owner could be: books show interest in studies, sports goods show interest in games. Then the real owner tells whether the guess was correct or not.

Why Is History Difficult?

  • Bags in which the things are clear and recognisable are easy to explain; those with few or unknown things are difficult.
  • Different people make different estimates from the same things, so disagreement arises.
  • The history exercise is difficult because the historian has to estimate from incomplete information.

Writing the Report

The report of the exercise (not more than one page) has three parts: first, the method of the exercise; second, the results — which guesses turned out correct and which wrong; third, the lesson — historians too estimate in the same way from incomplete information.

mcqs.q: Historians judge historical information on the basis of _______.
options: The greatest amount of collected information
mcqs.why: Information can be judged on the basis of the greatest amount of collected information. The more information a historian collects, the better the estimate that can be made.

mcqs.q: When a historical site is excavated, the samples are kept with _______ so that it is known where each was received.
mcqs.why: After making the samples, they are kept with informative titles from which it appears where they were received. This tells the historian how the samples are related to each other.

mcqs.q: From a single sample, a historian can obtain _______.
mcqs.why: From a single thing, for example a pencil, only a clue about its owner is obtained; much cannot be told with certainty. Many samples together give more understanding.

mcqs.q: Why can historians estimate more from many samples than from one?
options: Things found together explain each other and give more information
mcqs.why: When many things are found together, more things can be understood from them. A group of samples received together lets the historian guess much more than a single sample.

mcqs.q: In the bag exercise, sports goods in a bag show the owner's interest in _______.
mcqs.why: In the bag exercise, books show interest in studies and sports goods show interest in games. Students guess the owner from such clues, just as historians guess from samples.

mcqs.q: Why do some bags prove easier to explain than others?
options: Their things are clear and recognisable
mcqs.why: Bags in which the things are clear and recognisable are easy to explain. Bags in which things are few or unknown are difficult to explain.

mcqs.q: Why does disagreement arise in explaining samples?
options: Because different people make different estimates from the same things
mcqs.why: When people use specific things to estimate, different people reach different estimates, so disagreement arises. The same happens with historians examining samples.

mcqs.q: The history exercise is difficult because the historian has to estimate from _______.
mcqs.why: The historian has to estimate from incomplete information, because the past cannot be seen directly. That is why history skills need careful collection and judgement of information.

mcqs.q: The report of the history exercise should not be more than _______.
options: Half a page of one line
mcqs.why: The report on the method and results of the exercise should not be more than one page. It includes the method, the results, and the lesson learnt.

mcqs.q: What is the third part of the report of the bag exercise?
options: The lesson — historians too estimate from incomplete information
mcqs.why: The report has three parts: the method of the exercise, the results (which guesses were correct and which wrong), and the lesson that historians too estimate in the same way from incomplete information.

lessons.title: Geography Skills
lessons.notes_html:
Aerial Photographs and Ground Photographs

An aerial photograph is taken from above (from an aeroplane), while a ground photograph is taken from the front at ground level. In the aerial photograph things appear from above, and in the ground photograph from the front.

What Each Photograph Tells Us

Aerial photographGround photograph
The map-like view of a large area; the arrangement of roads; the shape of the land and buildings from aboveThe height and detail of buildings; how things actually look from the front

Students match the aerial photographs of the same place with the ground-level photographs and record their observations in two columns: what appeared in the aerial photograph, and what appeared in the ground photograph.

What Cannot Be Known from Aerial Photographs

From an aerial or satellite image, the condition inside a building, the names and thoughts of people, and small things cannot be known. For that, ground observation and asking people is necessary.

Comparing Our Own Map with Google Maps

Students first make the map of their school themselves. Then they compare it with the satellite image in Google Maps — writing the similarities (place of buildings, roads) and the differences (detail, scale) of both pictures.

mcqs.q: In an aerial photograph, things appear _______.
mcqs.why: An aerial photograph is taken from a high place, so things appear from above. In a ground photograph, the same things appear from the front.

mcqs.q: From an aerial photograph we can know _______.
options: The map of a large area and the arrangement of roads
mcqs.why: From an aerial photograph the map of a large area and the arrangement of roads is known. The inside of buildings and the names and thoughts of people cannot be known from it.

mcqs.q: From a ground photograph we can know _______.
options: The height and detail of buildings
The arrangement of all roads of a city
mcqs.why: From a ground photograph the height and detail of buildings is known, because it shows things from the front. A large area's arrangement is better seen in an aerial photograph.

mcqs.q: What cannot be known from an aerial or satellite image?
options: The condition inside a building and small things
mcqs.why: The condition inside a building, the names and thoughts of people, and small things cannot be known from an aerial or satellite image. For that, ground observation and asking people is necessary.

mcqs.q: In the observation record sheet, the two columns are for _______.
options: What appeared in the aerial photograph and what appeared in the ground photograph
mcqs.why: Observations are recorded in two columns: what appeared in the aerial photograph and what appeared in the ground photograph. Comparing both explains what information each type of photograph gives.

mcqs.q: The act of taking photographs of the ground from a high place is called _______.
mcqs.why: Taking photographs of the ground level from a high place is called aerial photography. Such photographs show the shape of the land and buildings in detail.

mcqs.q: Before comparing with Google Maps, students should first _______.
options: Make the map of their school themselves
mcqs.why: Students first make the map of their school themselves, so that they become able to make their own map. Then they compare it with the satellite image and discuss the similarities and differences.

mcqs.q: In comparing our own map with the satellite image, the similarities are _______.
mcqs.why: The similarities between the students' map and the satellite image are the place of buildings and roads. The differences are in detail and scale.

mcqs.q: Which difference is found between a self-made map and a satellite image?
mcqs.why: The self-made map and the satellite image differ in detail and scale. Discussing these similarities and differences is the purpose of the activity.

mcqs.q: To know the things that an aerial photograph cannot show, we need _______.
options: More photographs of the same type
mcqs.why: Ground observation and asking people is necessary for knowing what aerial photographs cannot show, such as the inside of buildings and small things. Geography skills use both photographs and field observation.

lessons.title: Continuing Map Study and Interpretation
lessons.notes_html:
Urban and Rural Settlements on the Map

Looking at the map of Asia, we write where urban settlements are dense — for example, on the banks of rivers and in coastal areas — and where rural settlements are spread.

Urban settlement (city)Rural settlement (village)Common to both
Big buildings, dense population, factoriesFields, open space, low population, animalsSchool, shop, people

The Venn Diagram

An equal diagram (Venn diagram) is made of two overlapping circles. In one circle we write only the city's things (factories, big buildings), in the other only the village's things (fields, animals), and in the middle common part the common things of both (school, shop, people).

Questions We Answer from the Map

  • Identify the most important urban and rural settlements from the map.
  • Enter the information obtained from the map in a pie chart.
  • Record the analysis of the settlement patterns.
  • Determine the reasons for the different settlements on the map.
  • Determine the population density after studying the map.
  • Explain the differences in the settlements together with the latitude and longitude of nearby cities.

Why Do Settlements Become Dense?

Settlements become dense because of water, fertile land and trade. That is why the biggest urban settlements are found on the banks of rivers and in coastal areas, while settlements in deserts and mountains remain scattered.

mcqs.q: On the map of Asia, urban settlements are dense _______.
options: On the banks of rivers and in coastal areas
mcqs.why: Urban settlements are dense on the banks of rivers and in coastal areas. Water, fertile land and trade attract people to settle in such places.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a characteristic of an urban settlement?
options: Big buildings, dense population and factories
mcqs.why: A city has big buildings, dense population and factories. Fields, open space and low population are characteristics of a rural settlement (village).

mcqs.q: Which of these is a characteristic of a rural settlement?
options: Fields, open space and low population
mcqs.why: A village has fields, open space and low population. People there are mostly connected with farming and animals.

mcqs.q: In a Venn diagram of urban and rural settlements, the middle common part contains _______.
options: Common things of both, like school, shop and people
mcqs.why: In the Venn diagram, one circle holds only the city's things and the other only the village's things. The overlapping middle part holds the common things of both, such as school, shop and people.

mcqs.q: Settlements become dense because of _______.
mcqs.why: Settlements become dense because of water, fertile land and trade. These are the reasons for the different settlement patterns seen on the map.

mcqs.q: Population density means _______.
options: The number of cities in a country
How many people live in an area
mcqs.why: Population density tells how many people live in an area. After studying the map, students determine the population density of different areas.

mcqs.q: The information obtained from the map of settlements can be shown in a _______.
mcqs.why: The information obtained from the map is entered in a pie chart to show the share of each type of settlement. Map study includes recording and presenting information in such forms.

mcqs.q: To explain the differences in settlements, we also use the _______ of nearby cities.
mcqs.why: The differences in the settlements are explained together with the latitude and longitude of nearby cities. Latitude and longitude fix the exact position of a place on the map.

mcqs.q: In the group word activity, the 'rural' group writes about _______.
options: Fields, open space and low population
mcqs.why: The 'rural' group writes the characteristics of a village: fields, open space and low population. The 'urban' group writes big buildings, dense population and factories.

mcqs.q: Why are settlements in deserts and mountains scattered?
options: Because water and fertile land are scarce there
mcqs.why: Settlements become dense where water, fertile land and trade are available. In deserts and mountains these are scarce, so settlements remain spread out and scattered.

lessons.title: Interpretation of Material
lessons.notes_html:
Reading and Making Graphs

Material (data) is presented in graphs so that it can be understood at a glance. In this chapter we learn four forms: the line graph, the vertical bar graph, the pie chart and the pictograph.

The Line Graph

Years are written on the horizontal axis and the numbers on the vertical axis, starting from zero with equal intervals. A point is placed for each year, the points are joined with a solid line, and the graph is given a title.

Year2010201120122013201420152016
Daily biryanis150157120270526650480

Trend: from 2010 to 2012 the number remained almost the same; after 2012 the demand increased rapidly — from 120 in 2012 to the highest, 650, in 2015 — and then decreased to 480 in 2016. Possible reasons for annual change: increase in the fame of the centre, increase in population, change in prices, effect of weather or festivals, and competition or price increase for the decrease.

The Vertical Bar Graph

  • The names of the items (for example, games) are written on the horizontal axis, below the graph.
  • The numbers (for example, number of students) are written on the vertical axis, on the left side, starting from zero with equal intervals.
  • A bar is made for each item, as high as its number — the tallest bar shows the most liked item.
  • The graph has a title, for example "Our Favourite Games", and the vertical axis has a title, for example "Number of Students".

Ice-cream sales by month also show a trend: May about 50, June about 110, July about 330 (the highest, in hot weather), August about 210, September about 30.

The Pie Chart

In a pie chart, the total quantity is divided into slices of a circle, and the share of each part is shown. Share = number of that type ÷ total number × 100. In the book's "What we ate yesterday" pie chart: meat 43%, ice cream 29%, vegetables 14%, double roti 14%. Different colours are given to different slices, with a colour key (legend) beside the chart.

The Pictograph

In a pictograph, pictures are used in place of numbers. Example — ice-cream cones sold: Monday 4, Tuesday 2, Wednesday 3, Thursday 5, Friday 7, Saturday 1. Field observations (birds, cats, flowers, trees, dogs, buildings counted on a walk) can also be converted into a pictograph, with one picture for each thing counted.

mcqs.q: In a line graph, the years are written on the _______ axis.
mcqs.why: In a line graph, the years (2010 to 2016) are written on the horizontal axis. The numbers are written on the vertical axis, starting from zero with equal intervals.

mcqs.q: In the biryani line graph, the highest number of daily biryanis was in _______.
mcqs.why: The number of daily biryanis was highest in 2015 at 650. In 2016 it decreased to 480.

mcqs.q: What is the most important trend in the biryani material?
options: After 2012 the demand increased rapidly, then decreased a little in 2016
mcqs.why: The most important trend is that after 2012 the demand for biryanis increased rapidly — from 120 in 2012 to 650 in 2015 — and then there was some decrease in 2016.

mcqs.q: In 2012, the number of daily biryanis was _______.
mcqs.why: In 2012 the number of daily biryanis was 120, the lowest of the seven years. From 2013 onwards it rose quickly: 270, 526 and 650.

mcqs.q: After joining the points of a line graph, what must be done?
options: Give the graph a title and explain it through the material
mcqs.why: The points are joined with a solid line, the graph is given a title, for example 'Daily Biryanis of the Karachi Biryani Centre (2010–2016)'. Then the graph is explained in words through the material.

mcqs.q: Which can be a reason for the annual change in orders?
options: Increase in the fame of the centre and increase in population
mcqs.why: Possible reasons for annual change are increase in the fame of the centre, increase in population, change in prices, and the effect of weather or festivals. The decrease in 2016 may be due to competition or price increase.

mcqs.q: In a vertical bar graph, the number of students is written on the _______ axis.
mcqs.why: In a vertical bar graph, the names of the games are written on the horizontal axis, and the number of students on the vertical axis on the left side. The numbers start from zero with equal intervals.

mcqs.q: How can we tell from a bar graph which game is liked the most?
mcqs.why: The game with the tallest bar is liked the most, because the height of each bar shows its number of votes. The height of the cricket bar tells how many students like cricket.

mcqs.q: In the ice-cream sales material, the most ice cream was sold in _______.
mcqs.why: The most ice cream was sold in July, about 330, because July is a very hot month. The least was sold in September, about 30.

mcqs.q: In a pie chart, the share of a part is calculated as _______.
options: Number of that type × total number
Total number − number of that type
Number of that type ÷ total number × 100
mcqs.why: Share = number of that type ÷ total number × 100. In a pie chart the total quantity is divided into slices of a circle according to these shares.

mcqs.q: In the 'What we ate yesterday' pie chart, the biggest share is of _______.
mcqs.why: In the pie chart, meat has the biggest share at 43%. Ice cream is 29%, and vegetables and double roti are 14% each.

mcqs.q: Why are different colours given to the slices of a pie chart?
options: So each type can be recognised, with a colour key (legend) beside it
mcqs.why: Different colours are given to different slices so that each type can be recognised easily. A colour key (legend) beside the chart tells which colour belongs to which type.

mcqs.q: In a pictograph, numbers are shown by _______.
mcqs.why: A pictograph uses pictures in place of numbers — for example, one ice-cream cone picture for each cone sold. Monday 4, Tuesday 2 and Friday 7 cones are shown with that many pictures.

mcqs.q: In the pictograph of ice-cream cones sold, the most cones were sold on _______.
mcqs.why: The most cones were sold on Friday — 7. The fewest were sold on Saturday — only 1.

mcqs.q: If the increasing trend of biryani demand continues, what will the centre need?
options: More material, more workers and a bigger place
mcqs.why: If the increase continues, the centre will need more material, more workers and a bigger place. If the decrease continues, there will be a need to reduce the price or improve the quality.

lessons.title: Violence
lessons.notes_html:
What is Violence?

Violence is that behaviour in which, from the position of a person or an institution, harm — physical, mental or sexual — is caused to another through the use of force. Whether violence is intentional or unintentional, it is a serious violation of basic human rights. Protection from violence is the basic right of every human.

Three Types of Violence

  • Physical violence — harm to the body.
  • Mental violence — harm to the mind and feelings.
  • Sexual violence — harm of a sexual nature.

How Can One Be Saved from Violence?

  • Develop the ability to refuse: if a person asks you to do something which does not seem proper to you, refuse.
  • Shout for help.
  • Run away from there or go to a safe place.
  • Definitely talk to a person whom you trust.
  • Recognise the difference between good touch and bad touch, and never hide a bad touch.

Effects on a Person Affected by Violence

Physical and mental effects fall on the affected person: feelings of shame and guilt, loss of self-confidence, hurt self-respect, feelings of disappointment, worry, fear and anger; thoughts of harming oneself, not getting sleep, becoming restless, laziness in work, difficulties in relations, and feelings of loneliness among other people.

True or False?

  • "It is not possible to escape violence." — Incorrect. One can escape by refusing, shouting, going to a safe place and telling a trusted person.
  • "There are no feelings in a person affected by violence." — Incorrect. There are many feelings, such as shame, fear, disappointment and anger.
  • "For escaping violence it is necessary to develop the ability to refuse." — Correct.

Share this information with your parents, brothers, sisters and friends, so that everyone can protect themselves.

mcqs.q: Violence is behaviour in which harm is caused to another through _______.
mcqs.why: Violence is that behaviour in which harm — physical, mental or sexual — is caused to another through the use of force. It is a serious violation of basic human rights.

mcqs.q: How many types of violence are there?
mcqs.why: Violence has three types: physical violence, mental violence and sexual violence. All three are harmful and against human rights.

mcqs.q: Whether violence is intentional or unintentional, it is a serious violation of _______.
mcqs.why: Violence, whether intentional or unintentional, is a serious violation of basic human rights. Protection from violence is the basic right of every human.

mcqs.q: If someone asks you to do something improper, what should you do first?
options: Refuse — develop the ability to refuse
mcqs.why: To be saved from violence, develop the ability to refuse. If a person asks you to do something which does not seem proper, refuse, shout, run to a safe place and tell a trusted person.

mcqs.q: A person affected by violence should definitely talk about it with a person _______.
mcqs.why: A person affected by violence should definitely talk about it with a person on whom he has trust. Hiding the matter increases the harm.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an effect on a person affected by violence?
options: Feelings of shame, fear, worry and loss of self-confidence
mcqs.why: The affected person suffers feelings of shame and guilt, loss of self-confidence, hurt self-respect, disappointment, worry, fear and anger. Sleep and work are also disturbed.

mcqs.q: 'It is not possible to escape violence.' This statement is _______.
options: Incorrect — one can escape by refusing, shouting, going to a safe place and telling a trusted person
mcqs.why: The statement is incorrect. Escape from violence is possible: refuse, shout, go to a safe place, and talk to a trusted person.

mcqs.q: Why must we recognise the difference between good touch and bad touch?
options: For protection from violence — and a bad touch must never be hidden
mcqs.why: Recognising the difference between good touch and bad touch is necessary for protection from violence. A bad touch should never be hidden; a trusted person must be told.

mcqs.q: Protection from violence is the basic _______ of every human.
mcqs.why: Protection from violence is the basic right of every human. That is why violence is a violation of human rights.

mcqs.q: What should you do with the safety information of this chapter?
options: Share it with parents, brothers, sisters and friends
mcqs.why: For your protection and to avoid harm, inform your parents, brothers and sisters about these things, and share them with younger siblings and friends. Sharing safety information protects everyone.

lessons.title: Unit 6 End Exercises
lessons.notes_html:
Key Terms of Unit 6

  • Aerial photography: the act of taking photographs of the ground level from a high place.
  • Supporting skills: those special methods of skill in which students are expected to play a role in learning the manners and etiquette of the class — students working together, cooperating, conversing and listening to one another for a common aim.
  • Decision-making: the practical method of collecting information, combining the alternatives of decisions and identifying them through the selection of a decision.
  • Pictograph: that method of presenting numerical material in which material of different types is compared by counting, using pictures.
  • The two basic graph forms of this unit are the line graph and the vertical bar graph.

Ortho-Photo and Photogrammetry

An ortho-photo map is that map which is made by correcting aerial photographs (removing the slant of their edges and the difference of height), so that it shows correct measurement and correct place like an ordinary map. The process of comparing and correcting different aerial photographs is called photogrammetry.

Why Decision-Making Skills Matter

Decision-making skills include identifying the problem, collecting information, considering alternative solutions and selecting the best solution. Through this, students learn to examine every matter thoughtfully (critical thinking) and learn to place their views before others with arguments.

Elements of the Rural-Urban Settlement Map

  • Settlements (cities and villages)
  • Roads and transport routes
  • Rivers and water sources
  • Fertile land
  • Latitude and longitude
  • The key of the map (explanation of symbols)

These maps are different from other maps because they show, instead of the shape of the land, the residence of people and the spread of settlements.

Line Graph and Pie Chart: The Difference

Line graphPie chart
Change with time is shown with a line (for example, the number of biryanis year by year)The total quantity is divided into slices of a circle and the share of each part is shown (for example, meat 43% in food)

Solving Common Problems of the School

From a survey, select three common problems (for example: cleanliness, shortage of water, lack of a playground). Form an action committee and use the steps of problem-solving: identify the problem, collect information, think of alternative solutions, select the best solution. Then make a poster of the causes and solution and publish it in the school newsletter.

mcqs.q: The act of taking photographs of the ground level from a high place is called _______.
mcqs.why: Taking photographs of the ground level from a high place is called aerial photography. The process of comparing and correcting different aerial photographs is called photogrammetry.

mcqs.q: The special methods by which students learn together and play a role in the manners of the class are called _______ skills.
mcqs.why: Supporting skills are those special methods in which students work together — cooperating, conversing and listening to one another for a common aim. They help students learn together and fulfil shared responsibility.

mcqs.q: The practical method of collecting information, considering alternatives and selecting a decision is called _______.
mcqs.why: Decision-making is the practical method of collecting information, combining the alternatives of decisions and identifying them through the selection of a decision. It develops critical thinking in students.

mcqs.q: The method of presenting numerical material by comparing different types through counting, using pictures, is called a _______.
mcqs.why: A pictograph is the method of presenting numerical material in which different types are compared by counting, with the use of pictures. Each picture stands for a counted thing.

mcqs.q: The two basic graph forms taught in Unit 6 are the line graph and the _______.
mcqs.why: The two types are the line graph and the vertical bar graph. In Chapter 6 these are the two basic graph forms taught for showing material.

mcqs.q: An ortho-photo map is made by _______.
options: Correcting aerial photographs — removing the slant of edges and difference of height
mcqs.why: An ortho-photo map is made by correcting aerial photographs, so that it shows correct measurement and correct place like an ordinary map. Comparing and correcting aerial photographs is photogrammetry.

mcqs.q: Decision-making skills help students develop _______.
mcqs.why: Decision-making — identifying the problem, collecting information, considering alternatives and selecting the best solution — develops critical thinking. Students also learn to place their views before others with arguments.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an element of the rural-urban settlement map?
options: Settlements, roads, rivers, fertile land, latitude and longitude, and the key of the map
mcqs.why: The elements of the rural-urban settlement map are settlements, roads and transport routes, rivers and water sources, fertile land, latitude and longitude, and the key of the map. These maps show the residence of people rather than the shape of the land.

mcqs.q: Settlement maps are different from other maps because they show _______.
options: The residence of people and the spread of settlements
mcqs.why: Settlement maps show, instead of the shape of the land, the residence of people and the spread of settlements. That is what makes them different from physical maps.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a line graph and a pie chart?
options: A line graph shows change with time; a pie chart divides the total into slices showing each part's share
A line graph shows shares of a total; a pie chart shows change with time
A pie chart has no numbers
mcqs.why: In a line graph, change with time is shown with a line, for example the number of biryanis year by year. In a pie chart, the total quantity is divided into slices of a circle showing the share of each part, for example meat 43% in food.
